tasks.short: Create still and animated graphics for news broadcasts.

steps.what: Read the news brief, deadline, script and required graphic formats.

loop.input: News brief, script and broadcast specification.
loop.output: Structured graphic requirements with source passages and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate required fields and formats; designer confirms names, figures and editorial intent.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction; unresolved fields return to the producer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text scripts describe graphics inconsistently; fixed forms can replace this loop when adopted.

steps.what: Collect approved images, logos, footage and data from the project folders.
Choose the visual explanation, composition and emphasis.
Build still graphics in graphics editing software.
Animate graphics and render sequences in motion graphics software.
Check exported files against technical requirements in broadcast quality-control software.
Approve factual accuracy, editorial framing and readability of the broadcast proof.
Load approved graphics into broadcast playout software and confirm rundown placement.

tasks.design: An intake flow in {WORKFLOW} turns briefs into confirmed requirements and retrieves approved assets from {DOCS}. Configured templates in {OTHER} graphics and animation software produce repeatable formats; a deterministic job checks exports and prepares the playout package. Editorial approval and the broadcast operator's release check remain separate gates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates, asset folders and playout specifications were disconnected. Bespoke editorial graphics also need substantial visual judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing template engines and file checks handle repeatable production. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building adapters; a bounded extraction loop can read informal briefs.
tasks.still_hard: Breaking news, misleading visual emphasis, custom animation and proprietary playout interfaces. Technical checks cannot establish editorial truth.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a visual explanation that is accurate, legible under time pressure and proportionate to the story.

ambition.what: A same-day visual explainer service for the editorial team.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time collecting assets and rebuilding recurring formats. They can recommend which stories merit an explainer; editorial selection and broadcast release rights stay with their existing roles.

reach.task: Shape the visual explanation of a complex news story.
reach.learn: Editorial verification, source attribution and how graphics can distort a claim.

reach.task: Adapt an approved explainer for a small-screen audience.
reach.learn: Responsive composition, accessible contrast and motion accessibility.

evidence.claim: Locked templates and structured variant inputs can reduce recurring graphic production work; broadcast suitability requires testing.
Brief extraction, asset assembly and technical export checks can be separated from editorial decisions.
Creative selection and editorial approval remain human; no autonomous agent is necessary.

assumptions: This specialist task applies to a mid-size broadcaster or an organisation with an in-house broadcast team.
The team already uses graphics, motion graphics and playout software, represented by {OTHER}.
Recurring formats form a meaningful share of production, while custom concepts remain manual.
Creation mainly happens on system screens; the supplied meeting-heavy means prior does not fit this task.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
Access estimates include permission setup; consultation under national rules may add elapsed time if employee monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Which recurring formats can use locked templates?
Do the installed tools support scripted rendering, imports and playout integration?
Who currently authorises editorial content and final release?
What rights and personal-data restrictions apply to the asset library?
research_questions: Which technical failures can the installed broadcast tools detect automatically?
Can an approved file version be bound reliably to its rundown entry and approval record?
new_work: Resolve missing brief fields and unavailable assets.
Review failed technical checks and integration failures.
Test template changes before live use.

tasks.short: Create photographic proofs of physical layouts for supervisors or clients.

steps.what: Select the layout version and decide whether a photograph or direct export is needed.
Position the physical layout, camera, lighting and colour reference.
Photograph the layout and check focus, reflections and framing.
Crop photographs, apply colour settings and assemble labelled proofs in image editing software.
Send the selected proof to the supervisor or client.

tasks.design: Use direct export from {OTHER} design software whenever the proof concerns a digital layout, eliminating photography for that branch. For physical layouts, configure camera presets and batch proof preparation in {OTHER} image editing software, then store versioned proofs in {DOCS}. A configured {WORKFLOW} sends the selected version through {EMAIL} after the designer confirms the proof and recipient.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical appearance cannot be recovered from a digital source alone. Proof preparation and delivery often rely on individual presets and informal file naming.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing camera presets, batch image processing and approval flows cover most repeatable work. Small adapters can connect filenames, versions and proof requests without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Reflective surfaces, textured materials, colour fidelity and showing physical scale. A photograph does not replace a calibrated print or material sample.
tasks.human_edge: Decide what a reviewer must see and capture the material honestly.

ambition.what: A remote material-proof pack showing finish, scale and detail.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time processing and sending proofs, while physical setup remains substantial. They can propose a proof method suited to the decision; client acceptance rights do not change.

reach.task: Prepare a versioned proof pack for production review.
reach.learn: Colour profiles, proof limitations and consistent production annotations.

evidence.claim: Digital source exports can eliminate photographing a screen or flat digital layout.
Physical capture still needs human control of lighting, reflections and material presentation.
Configured presets and batch processing can prepare consistent photographic proofs without generative editing.

assumptions: In a typical mid-size marketing team, digital layouts usually use direct exports; this supplemental camera task concerns physical layouts or mockups.
Time shares describe the physical-photography branch. Digital cases bypass setup and capture entirely.
Camera settings are configured on equipment; no separate software slot is assumed for physical capture.
Automated processing preserves material appearance and does not generate missing visual detail.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates.
The starter uses existing equipment and introduces no employee monitoring; applicable national consultation rules still need checking.
unknowns: How many proof requests actually require physical photography?
Are digital source files available for the remaining requests?
Which colour standards and camera equipment are already used?
Does the client need a photographic proof, a calibrated print or a physical sample?
research_questions: Which installed image editing features support repeatable crops, colour profiles and proof labels?
Can existing proof delivery preserve version history and recipient permissions?
new_work: Maintain capture presets and proof templates.
Review automated crops and colour processing.
Resolve incorrect source versions and delivery permissions.
Periodically check the capture setup against a reference sample.

tasks.short: Write and edit client copy to fit the brief, brand and layout.

steps.what: Read the client brief and clarify audience, message, tone and constraints.

loop.input: Copy brief, client comments and layout specification.
loop.output: Structured copy requirements and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require audience, purpose, format and length; designer confirms inferred requirements.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction; ask the requester about unresolved or conflicting instructions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Informal briefs contain implicit instructions; a complete structured intake form would remove this loop.

steps.what: Find approved facts, previous copy and brand guidance in the document store.
Write headline, body copy and calls to action in the copy document.

loop.input: Confirmed requirements, approved source pack and brand guidelines.
loop.output: Copy draft with claim-to-source references and flagged gaps.
loop.check: Check length, required wording and prohibited terms deterministically; require references for factual claims.
loop.stop: One draft and at most two repair passes; unresolved claims remain flagged for the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Original phrasing and adaptation to audience require language generation; fixed approved copy should use templates.

steps.what: Edit for meaning, factual support, brand voice and fit within the layout.
Approve the message and claims, or return requested changes.
Send the approved copy version to the client or publishing colleague.

tasks.design: A portable intake and approval flow in {WORKFLOW} assembles an approved source pack from {DOCS} and uses bounded loops to structure informal briefs and draft copy. Deterministic checks enforce length and required wording, while the designer edits meaning, claims and layout fit. Approval binds the exact version and recipient before {WORKFLOW} delivers it through {EMAIL}; publishing is a separate action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Free-text briefs, scattered facts and subjective brand voice made end-to-end rules brittle. Approval emails also failed to identify the final version reliably.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can use supplied source material, while existing document and workflow features handle versions, checks and approvals. Small integrations are cheaper to build with AI-assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: Persuasive judgement, unsupported source claims, ambiguous client feedback and regulated wording. Source references help review but do not prove a claim is true.
tasks.human_edge: Find the message the audience will understand and trust, then challenge claims or phrasing that weaken it.

ambition.what: A weekly headline-test decision with the campaign team.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends more time editing the message and testing its fit with the visual concept. They can propose headline tests with a search marketing strategist; budget and final claim approval rights stay with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Develop a campaign message and supporting copy.
reach.learn: Interviewing for a brief, narrative structure and evidence-based editing.

reach.task: Choose headline variants for a campaign test.
reach.learn: Test design, conversion measures and how to interpret small samples.

evidence.claim: A bounded drafting loop can combine supplied facts, brand instructions and layout constraints; editorial review remains necessary.
Version-bound approval, length checks and delivery are deterministic workflow functions.
The digest provides no documented copywriting case supporting a quantified saving for this task.

assumptions: The designer handles short commercial copy; specialist legal or technical writing requires the relevant reviewer.
A marketing manager approves routine client copy; contractual client approval can add a further gate.
Requested changes repeat editing and approval before delivery.
Source retrieval uses an approved project source list; the designer resolves missing or outdated facts.
Automatic delivery uses the recipient approved with the exact copy version.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates; the supplied automation prior is not a measured saving.
GDPR applies to personal data in briefs and drafts. National consultation rules may apply if the tool changes employee-data processing or enables monitoring.
Build ranges cover a starter with existing {DOCS}, {EMAIL} and {WORKFLOW} access; consultation can add elapsed time.
unknowns: Which copy types and claims require specialist or client approval?
Where are authoritative facts and approved wording maintained?
May client material be processed by the selected model service?
Which versioning, approval and delivery features are already configured?
What employee consultation or access approval is required?
research_questions: How accurately does source-linked drafting preserve claims and tone on representative briefs?
Can the existing approval mechanism bind document version, recipient and permitted delivery action?
Which copy categories are better served by approved templates than generation?
new_work: Review draft claims against authoritative sources.
Maintain brand guidance, approved wording and drafting instructions.
Resolve conflicting briefs and missing source facts.
Check approval-version mismatches and delivery failures.
Sample accepted drafts for recurring factual or tone errors.

role.altitude: The designer's week shifts toward visual explanation, material fidelity and message judgement. Production preparation and handoffs shrink; broader editorial, spending or publishing authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Work with Editors on evidence-backed visual explanations.
Work with Desktop Publishers on reliable production proofs.
Work with Search Marketing Strategists on headline tests.
skills_to_grow: Reusable graphic and motion template design.
Colour management and physical proof selection.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a compact campaign-production service that joins visual explainers, material proofs and testable copy, with named reviewers approving the relevant release actions.
